newsitem.title: USA: U.S. December T-bond finishes quiet day lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. December T-bond finishes quiet day lower.

text.p: U.S. December Treasury bond futures finished slightly lower after a session of very quiet trading, never fully recovering from a drop in the latest weekly jobless claims.
In view of lethargic action in the pits and a lack of any other economic news today, the weak jobless claims cast a shadow over the market all day, traders said.
Jobless claims fell to 320,000 in the October 19 week from a revised 342,000 in the previous week. The four-week average fell to 331,250 from a revised 336,250.
Traders said they needed the September durable goods report to rescue the market from recent stagnancy.

Durable goods orders, due Friday at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT, were forecast up 2.0 percent overall and up 1.3 percent excluding the defense sector. In August durables fell 3.2 percent overall and dropped 3.6 percent ex-defense.
Jobless claims lent the market a negative tone on Thursday, but overall the mood was indecisive and the market range-bound.
Dec T-bonds managed this week to hold above key support, but traders noted stiff resistance above the market.
Traders said the 111-00 handle sits above the market like daunting resistance. Technicians said a move below 109-26/32 or above 111-26/32 to 111-28/32 was needed to outline the market's direction.
Some bulls kept 112-00 to 114-00 targets for December T-bonds, but bears said the August 13 and October 4 highs at 111-26/32 and 111-28/32 were beginning to look like a double top formation.
March Eurodollars were trapped in a 94.26 to 94.35 trading band and suffered from extremely light volume all week.
Traders said some sessions this week saw about half of the normal trading volume.

At settlement, December T-bonds were down 8/32 to 110-19/32, 10-year notes were off 1/32 at 108-10/32, muni-bonds lost 20/32 to 113-31/32 and March Eurodollars were unchanged at 94.29. March T-bills were up one basis point 94.29. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
